title: Twenty-two years, 34 moments
lede: From one store in Oregon to a blog. Filter by thread.

events.title: Hollywood Entertainment incorporated
events.text: Mark J. Wattles founds the company in Oregon.

events.title: First Hollywood Video store opens
events.text: The first store opens four months after incorporation.

events.title: Initial public offering
events.text: The company goes public. It ends the year with 25 stores and revenue of $17.3M.

events.title: 113 stores
events.text: Hollywood opens 33 stores and acquires 55 in one year.

events.title: Video Watch bought
events.text: The assets of 42 Video Watch superstores are acquired for about $60.3M. The year ends with 305 stores in 23 states.

events.title: 250 openings in a year
events.text: The chain reaches 551 stores in 29 states and plans at least 300 more for 1997.

events.title: 907 stores
events.text: Revenue passes $500M. Long-term obligations reach $233.5M.

events.title: Reel.com acquired
events.text: Hollywood buys the online video retailer for about $96.9M. Wattles leaves his full-time post to run it.

events.title: Revenue sharing and DVD
events.text: Revenue-sharing agreements with studios begin, and DVDs go on rental in most stores.

events.title: First annual loss
events.text: A net loss of $50.5M on revenue of $763.9M.

events.title: Game Crazy
events.text: 67 game departments are open inside Hollywood Video stores by year end. The chain has 1,615 stores.

events.title: Reel.com files to go public
events.text: A registration statement for a Reel.com offering is filed. The offering does not happen.

events.title: Rentrak settlement
events.text: Hollywood pays Rentrak about $14.0M and issues 200,000 shares to settle a suit over revenue sharing.

events.title: Reel.com’s store closed
events.text: The e-commerce business is shut down. About 200 of 240 employees are dismissed the next day. The charge is $69.3M.

events.title: Wattles returns
events.text: The founder returns full time to Hollywood.

events.title: Stores written down
events.text: Same-store sales fall for the first time in 21 quarters. An impairment charge of $74.3M follows.

events.title: Going-concern warning
events.text: The company is in violation of its credit covenants. Its auditors cite substantial doubt about its ability to continue.

events.title: A new contract for the founder
events.text: Wattles receives 3 million shares, worth $3.27M that day, under a new employment agreement.

events.title: Recovery
events.text: Net income of $259.7M, as restated, and long-term obligations down to $388.7M.

events.title: Leonard Green buyout at $14.00
events.text: Hollywood agrees to be taken private by an affiliate of Leonard Green & Partners.

events.title: Price cut to $10.25
events.text: The merger agreement is amended and Hollywood is allowed to seek other bids.

events.title: Blockbuster proposes $11.50
events.text: Blockbuster writes that it is prepared to make an all-cash offer.

events.title: Movie Gallery proposes $11.00
events.text: A written proposal arrives from the Alabama chain.

events.title: Movie Gallery signs at $13.25
events.text: Hollywood ends the Leonard Green agreement, paying $4.0M of expenses, and signs with Movie Gallery.

events.title: Blockbuster raises to $14.50; Wattles resigns
events.text: Blockbuster offers $11.50 in cash and $3.00 in stock. Wattles resigns as chairman and CEO.

events.title: Blockbuster withdraws
events.text: Blockbuster lets its hostile offer expire amid antitrust resistance.

events.title: Merger completed
events.text: Hollywood becomes a subsidiary of Movie Gallery in a deal valued at about $1.25B including debt.

events.title: $522.95M goodwill impairment
events.text: Movie Gallery reports a net loss of $552.7M for its first year with Hollywood.

events.title: Trademark written down
events.text: The Hollywood trademark is impaired by $95.4M and $60.5M, to $15.0M.

events.title: Movie Gallery’s first Chapter 11
events.text: The company and its U.S. subsidiaries file in Richmond, Virginia.

events.title: Emergence
events.text: Movie Gallery leaves bankruptcy. Old shares are canceled. Sopris Capital affiliates control 86.3% of the votes by late 2008.

events.title: Second Chapter 11
events.text: About 760 stores begin closing at once. 545 Hollywood Video stores remain.

events.title: Liquidation
events.text: Movie Gallery tells the court it will close its remaining stores. A judge approves on May 19.

events.title: Brands sent to auction
events.text: The estate submits a plan to auction its intellectual property, including Reel.com, through StreamBank.
